name: Malaria
description: A mosquito-borne infection caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
keySymptoms: cyclical fever
chills with rigors
recent travel to endemic area
riskFactors: living in or travel to malaria-endemic area
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical assessment and laboratory testing (blood smear or rapid diagnostic test) promptly for any fever in a malaria-endemic area, especially if symptoms are severe or worsening.
prevention: antimalarial chemoprevention in pregnancy where indicated
notes: One of the leading causes of outpatient visits in Kenya; risk varies greatly by altitude and region, with western Kenya and coastal areas being higher-risk.

name: HIV/AIDS
description: A viral infection that attacks the immune system (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), which if untreated can progress to Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS).
keySymptoms: unexplained significant weight loss
recurrent opportunistic infections
persistent swollen lymph nodes
whenToSeekCare: Anyone with risk factors or suggestive symptoms should seek confidential HIV testing and counselling; early diagnosis and treatment substantially improve outcomes.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher prevalence reported in certain counties, particularly around Lake Victoria region
differentialConditions: other causes of chronic weight loss
notes: Kenya has an established national HIV testing and antiretroviral therapy program; stigma remains a barrier to testing and care.

name: Tuberculosis
description: A bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, most commonly affecting the lungs but can affect other organs.
keySymptoms: cough lasting more than two weeks
night sweats with weight loss
coughing up blood
riskFactors: close contact with a TB patient
whenToSeekCare: Anyone with a cough lasting more than two weeks, especially with weight loss or night sweats, should seek evaluation and sputum testing at a health facility.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk in overcrowded urban settlements
prevention: treatment of latent TB in high-risk groups
notes: Kenya is among countries with a high TB burden; TB-HIV co-infection is an important consideration.

name: Typhoid Fever
description: A systemic bacterial infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually transmitted through contaminated food or water.
keySymptoms: stepwise rising fever over several days
relative bradycardia
abdominal tenderness
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care for fever persisting more than 3 days, especially with abdominal pain, as laboratory testing and prompt treatment reduce complications.
notes: A common cause of prolonged fever in Kenya; often clinically confused with malaria.

name: Cholera
description: An acute diarrheal illness caused by Vibrio cholerae bacteria, spread through contaminated water or food, capable of causing rapid severe dehydration.
keySymptoms: large-volume watery ('rice-water') stool
rapid onset dehydration
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for profuse watery diarrhea with signs of dehydration; oral or intravenous rehydration is urgently needed.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: outbreak-prone areas with poor water and sanitation infrastructure
differentialConditions: other acute bacterial or viral gastroenteritis
prevention: cholera vaccination during outbreak response where available
notes: Occurs in periodic outbreaks in Kenya, often associated with flooding or disrupted water systems.

name: Shigellosis (Bacterial Dysentery)
description: An intestinal infection caused by Shigella bacteria, characterized by diarrhea that is often bloody, spread via the fecal-oral route.
keySymptoms: bloody or mucoid diarrhea
high frequency small-volume stools
whenToSeekCare: Seek care if diarrhea is bloody, persistent, or accompanied by signs of dehydration or high fever.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: areas with limited access to clean water and sanitation
notes: An important cause of bloody diarrhea in children in Kenya.

name: Amoebiasis
description: An intestinal infection caused by the parasite Entamoeba histolytica, transmitted through contaminated food or water.
keySymptoms: intermittent diarrhea alternating with constipation
abdominal tenderness
warningSigns: signs of liver abscess (right upper abdominal pain with fever)
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent or recurrent diarrhea, especially with blood or mucus in stool.
notes: Can occasionally spread beyond the gut to cause liver abscess, which requires prompt evaluation.

name: Giardiasis
description: An intestinal infection caused by the parasite Giardia lamblia, often linked to contaminated water sources.
keySymptoms: foul-smelling greasy diarrhea
prolonged bloating
whenToSeekCare: Seek care if diarrhea persists more than a week or is associated with weight loss.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: areas relying on untreated surface water
notes: A common cause of prolonged, non-bloody diarrhea.

name: Schistosomiasis (Bilharzia)
description: A parasitic disease caused by blood flukes (Schistosoma species), acquired through contact with freshwater contaminated by infected snails.
keySymptoms: blood in urine (urogenital form)
chronic abdominal symptoms after freshwater exposure
riskFactors: swimming or wading in freshwater lakes or rivers
warningSigns: signs of liver or kidney involvement
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing if there is a history of freshwater contact along with urinary or gastrointestinal symptoms.
prevention: improved sanitation to reduce water contamination
notes: One of the neglected tropical diseases with significant burden around Lake Victoria.

name: Soil-Transmitted Helminthiasis
description: Intestinal worm infections (including roundworm, hookworm, and whipworm) transmitted through contact with soil contaminated by human feces.
keySymptoms: chronic abdominal discomfort in a child with poor growth
iron deficiency anemia in endemic area
whenToSeekCare: Seek care for persistent abdominal symptoms or unexplained anemia, especially in children in endemic areas.
differentialConditions: other causes of abdominal pain in children
notes: Deworming programs in schools are a key public health strategy in Kenya.

name: Hepatitis A
description: A viral liver infection transmitted through contaminated food or water, usually self-limiting.
keySymptoms: jaundice with recent gastrointestinal upset
dark urine
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation if jaundice develops or symptoms are severe or prolonged.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: areas with limited access to safe water and sanitation
notes: Usually self-limiting in children but can cause more severe illness in adults.

name: Hepatitis B
description: A viral liver infection that can be acute or chronic, transmitted through blood, unprotected sex, or from mother to child.
keySymptoms: chronic fatigue with abnormal liver findings
jaundice
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing if there are risk factors or symptoms suggestive of liver disease; chronic infection requires ongoing specialist monitoring.
notes: Chronic hepatitis B can lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer if untreated; vaccination is part of Kenya's infant immunization schedule.

name: Dengue Fever
description: A viral infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, causing an acute febrile illness that can occasionally become severe.
keySymptoms: sudden high fever with severe joint and muscle pain
rash appearing after a few days of fever
riskFactors: living in or travel to an area with Aedes mosquito activity
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical assessment for high fever with severe body aches, and urgent care if warning signs of severe dengue appear.
notes: Outbreaks have been reported in coastal and some urban areas of Kenya.

name: Chikungunya
description: A viral infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, characterized by fever and pronounced joint pain.
keySymptoms: severe, often disabling joint pain
fever with joint swelling
riskFactors: living in or travel to an area with Aedes mosquito activity
whenToSeekCare: Seek care for fever with severe joint pain, particularly if symptoms are worsening or persistent.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: coastal and urban areas with mosquito activity
notes: Joint pain can persist for weeks to months after the acute illness resolves.

name: Rabies
description: A viral infection of the nervous system, almost always fatal once symptoms appear, transmitted through the bite or scratch of an infected animal (commonly dogs).
keySymptoms: history of animal bite followed by neurological symptoms
hydrophobia
riskFactors: animal bite or scratch, especially from unvaccinated dogs
warningSigns: any animal bite with broken skin
agitation or confusion after a bite
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately after any bite or scratch from a suspect animal for wound care and post-exposure prophylaxis, before symptoms develop.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: areas with high stray dog populations
prevention: avoiding contact with stray or wild animals
prompt wound washing and post-exposure prophylaxis after any bite
notes: Once symptoms appear, rabies is almost universally fatal; prevention through prompt post-exposure treatment is critical.

name: Brucellosis
description: A bacterial zoonotic infection transmitted from livestock to humans, typically through unpasteurized dairy products or contact with infected animals.
keySymptoms: recurrent or undulating fever with animal or unpasteurized dairy exposure
riskFactors: occupational contact with livestock (farmers, herders, veterinarians)
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for prolonged unexplained fever, particularly with a history of livestock contact or unpasteurized dairy consumption.
prevention: pasteurization of milk and dairy products
notes: An occupational hazard among livestock keepers in pastoral regions of Kenya.

name: Leptospirosis
description: A bacterial infection transmitted through contact with water or soil contaminated by the urine of infected animals, particularly rodents.
keySymptoms: fever after exposure to floodwater or contaminated water with calf muscle tenderness
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care for fever after flood or contaminated water exposure, especially with muscle pain or jaundice.
notes: Often under-recognized; risk increases after flooding events.

name: Measles
description: A highly contagious viral infection, particularly serious in young or unvaccinated children.
keySymptoms: fever followed by a spreading rash starting on the face
conjunctivitis with cough and coryza
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care promptly, especially in unvaccinated children, as complications such as pneumonia can be serious.
prevention: measles vaccination (part of routine immunization schedule)
notes: Outbreaks can occur in communities with immunization gaps; vitamin A supplementation is part of clinical management in some settings.

name: Chickenpox (Varicella)
description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy blistering rash, common in childhood.
keySymptoms: rash progressing from spots to fluid-filled blisters to crusts
riskFactors: lack of prior infection or vaccination
close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Most cases can be managed at home; seek care if the rash becomes infected, breathing difficulty occurs, or fever is prolonged, especially in adults, pregnant women, or immunocompromised individuals.
prevention: isolation of infected individuals during infectious period
notes: Can be more severe in adults, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals.

name: Mumps
description: A viral infection primarily affecting the salivary glands, most common in children and young adults.
commonSymptoms: swelling of the jaw or cheek area
keySymptoms: painful swelling of one or both parotid glands
riskFactors: close contact in schools or crowded settings
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care if severe headache, neck stiffness, or testicular pain develops, as these may indicate complications.
notes: Complications can include meningitis, orchitis, or pancreatitis, though these are uncommon.

name: Bacterial Meningitis
description: A serious infection causing inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
keySymptoms: neck stiffness with fever and altered consciousness
non-blanching rash (in meningococcal disease)
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for fever with neck stiffness, severe headache, or altered consciousness.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: outbreak-prone in crowded or institutional settings
prevention: vaccination against relevant bacterial causes (e.g., meningococcus, pneumococcus, Hib) where available
notes: A medical emergency requiring urgent hospital-based treatment; rapid deterioration is possible.

name: Pneumonia (Community-Acquired)
description: An infection of the lungs, commonly caused by bacteria or viruses, leading to inflammation of the air sacs.
keySymptoms: productive cough with fever and rapid breathing
chest pain worsened by breathing
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for cough with fever and breathing difficulty, especially in young children or older adults.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk in areas with indoor air pollution from cooking fuels
notes: A leading cause of illness and death in young children in Kenya.

name: Influenza
description: A contagious viral respiratory infection causing seasonal outbreaks of fever, cough, and body aches.
keySymptoms: abrupt onset of fever with body aches and respiratory symptoms
whenToSeekCare: Most cases resolve with rest and supportive care; seek medical attention if breathing difficulty or high fever persists, especially in young children, older adults, or those with chronic illness.
notes: Symptoms overlap considerably with other respiratory viral illnesses.

name: COVID-19
description: A respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, with a wide range of severity from mild to critical illness.
keySymptoms: loss of taste or smell
progressive breathing difficulty
riskFactors: close contact with an infected person
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care if breathing difficulty, chest pain, or confusion develops; mild cases can generally be managed with rest and monitoring at home.
notes: Severity and dominant strains have changed over time; local health authority guidance should be followed.

name: Urinary Tract Infection
description: An infection of the urinary system, most commonly involving the bladder, caused predominantly by bacteria.
keySymptoms: painful urination with increased frequency and urgency
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for painful or frequent urination, and urgent care if fever, back pain, or vomiting develop, which may indicate kidney involvement.
notes: Recurrent infections may warrant further evaluation for underlying risk factors.

name: Syphilis
description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that progresses through distinct stages if untreated.
commonSymptoms: rash on palms and soles (secondary stage)
keySymptoms: painless genital ulcer
non-itchy rash involving palms and soles
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing and treatment promptly if a genital sore or unexplained rash appears, and for partners of anyone diagnosed.
prevention: antenatal screening to prevent congenital syphilis
notes: Untreated syphilis in pregnancy can cause serious harm to the fetus; antenatal screening is important.

name: Gonorrhea
description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that can affect the genital tract, rectum, and throat.
keySymptoms: purulent genital discharge with painful urination
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing and treatment for genital discharge or discomfort, and ensure partner treatment to prevent reinfection.
notes: Often coexists with chlamydia infection; can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility if untreated.

name: Chlamydia Infection
description: A common sexually transmitted bacterial infection that is frequently asymptomatic.
keySymptoms: often asymptomatic; discharge with dysuria when present
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing if there are symptoms or a partner has been diagnosed, since infection is often silent but can cause complications.
notes: A leading preventable cause of infertility when untreated due to its often silent course.

name: Trichomoniasis
description: A common sexually transmitted infection caused by a parasite, often causing genital irritation and discharge.
keySymptoms: frothy, foul-smelling discharge
genital itching
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation for unusual genital discharge or discomfort; partner treatment is also recommended.
notes: Can increase susceptibility to other sexually transmitted infections, including HIV.

name: Tinea (Fungal Skin Infection)
description: A common superficial fungal infection of the skin, scalp, or nails, often referred to as ringworm.
commonSymptoms: red circular rash with clear center
keySymptoms: ring-shaped itchy rash with a clearer center
riskFactors: close contact with infected individuals or animals
whenToSeekCare: Most cases can be managed with topical antifungal treatment; seek care if the rash spreads widely, does not improve, or shows signs of secondary infection.
notes: Very common in children, particularly scalp involvement (tinea capitis).

name: Scabies
description: A contagious skin infestation caused by microscopic mites, causing intense itching.
commonSymptoms: small bumps or burrows on skin
keySymptoms: itching that worsens at night
burrows between fingers or on wrists
riskFactors: close physical contact with an infected person
warningSigns: signs of widespread secondary bacterial infection
whenToSeekCare: Seek treatment for persistent intense itching with a rash, and treat close contacts simultaneously to prevent reinfestation.
prevention: avoiding close contact with infected individuals
washing bedding and clothing in hot water
notes: Highly contagious within households; simultaneous treatment of contacts is important to prevent recurrence.

name: Onchocerciasis (River Blindness)
description: A parasitic infection transmitted by blackflies that breed near fast-flowing rivers, which can cause skin and eye disease.
keySymptoms: intense itching with nodules in a person from a riverine blackfly-endemic area
riskFactors: living near fast-flowing rivers in endemic areas
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation for chronic itching with skin nodules in an endemic area, and urgent eye assessment if vision is affected.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: communities near fast-flowing rivers in endemic western Kenya
prevention: mass drug administration programs in endemic areas
notes: A neglected tropical disease targeted for elimination through community-based treatment programs.

name: Lymphatic Filariasis
description: A parasitic infection transmitted by mosquitoes that can cause chronic swelling of limbs or genitals (elephantiasis) over time.
lessCommonSymptoms: recurrent episodes of localized pain and swelling
keySymptoms: progressive, often asymmetric limb swelling in an endemic coastal area
warningSigns: signs of severe secondary bacterial infection
high fever with rapidly worsening swelling
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation for persistent limb or genital swelling, particularly with a history of residence in an endemic coastal area.
prevention: mass drug administration in endemic areas
notes: Chronic swelling (lymphedema) can cause significant disability and stigma; early management can limit progression.

name: Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar)
description: A parasitic infection transmitted by sandfly bites, affecting internal organs and causing prolonged fever and weight loss if untreated.
keySymptoms: prolonged fever with enlarged spleen and weight loss in an endemic area
riskFactors: living in or near semi-arid endemic regions
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for prolonged unexplained fever with weight loss and abdominal swelling in an endemic area, as specialized treatment is needed.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: semi-arid regions of northern and eastern Kenya
prevention: sandfly bite prevention (bed nets, insect repellent)
notes: Endemic to specific semi-arid regions of Kenya; requires specialized diagnosis and treatment.

name: Trachoma
description: A bacterial eye infection and a leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide, spread through contact and flies.
keySymptoms: chronic eye irritation with inward-turning eyelashes in advanced disease
whenToSeekCare: Seek eye examination for persistent eye irritation or discharge, particularly in children in endemic areas, to prevent long-term vision complications.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: arid and semi-arid regions with limited water access
notes: A leading preventable cause of blindness in affected communities; targeted for elimination through public health programs.

name: Hypertension
description: A chronic condition characterized by persistently elevated blood pressure, often with no symptoms until complications develop.
keySymptoms: blood pressure readings persistently above normal on repeated measurement
whenToSeekCare: Seek regular blood pressure screening; urgent care is needed if severe headache, chest pain, or vision changes occur.
notes: Often called a 'silent' condition because it can go undetected without regular screening; a major risk factor for stroke and heart disease.

name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
description: A chronic metabolic condition characterized by high blood glucose due to insulin resistance, often related to lifestyle and genetic factors.
keySymptoms: persistent excessive thirst and urination with elevated blood glucose
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue; urgent care is needed for confusion or severe dehydration.
notes: Increasingly common in Kenya alongside rising obesity and urbanization; regular monitoring reduces long-term complications.

name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
description: An autoimmune condition in which the body produces little or no insulin, usually presenting in childhood or young adulthood.
keySymptoms: rapid onset of thirst, urination and weight loss in a child or young person
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical evaluation for rapid weight loss with excessive thirst and urination in a child or young adult, as diabetic ketoacidosis can develop quickly.
prevention: no established prevention; early recognition and prompt treatment reduce complications
notes: Requires lifelong insulin therapy; diabetic ketoacidosis at presentation is a medical emergency.

name: Asthma
description: A chronic inflammatory condition of the airways causing episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, and cough.
keySymptoms: episodic wheezing and breathlessness triggered by specific factors
riskFactors: family history of asthma or allergies
warningSigns: inability to speak in full sentences
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care for severe breathlessness, and routine care for recurrent wheezing or cough to establish a management plan.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher symptom burden with indoor air pollution exposure
notes: A leading chronic respiratory condition in children; often underdiagnosed.

name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
description: A progressive lung disease characterized by long-term breathing difficulty, commonly linked to smoking or chronic exposure to indoor air pollution.
keySymptoms: progressive breathlessness with a long history of smoking or biomass smoke exposure
riskFactors: indoor air pollution from cooking fuels
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent cough and breathlessness, and urgent care for sudden worsening of breathing.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk with indoor biomass fuel use
notes: Under-recognized in settings with high biomass fuel use for cooking.

name: Coronary Artery Disease
description: A condition in which the blood vessels supplying the heart become narrowed, increasing the risk of chest pain and heart attack.
lessCommonSymptoms: pain radiating to the arm or jaw
keySymptoms: exertional chest pain relieved by rest
warningSigns: severe chest pain lasting more than a few minutes
pain radiating to arm, jaw, or back
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for severe or persistent chest pain, especially with breathlessness, sweating, or pain radiating to the arm or jaw.
notes: Increasingly recognized in Kenya alongside rising rates of hypertension and diabetes.

name: Heart Failure
description: A condition in which the heart is unable to pump blood effectively to meet the body's needs, often resulting from underlying heart or valve disease.
lessCommonSymptoms: rapid weight gain from fluid retention
keySymptoms: breathlessness on exertion or lying flat with leg swelling
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for breathlessness with leg swelling, and urgent care if symptoms worsen suddenly.
notes: Rheumatic heart disease remains an important cause of heart failure in younger patients in Kenya.

name: Stroke
description: A sudden interruption of blood supply to the brain, either from a blockage or bleeding, leading to loss of brain function.
keySymptoms: sudden onset of one-sided weakness, facial droop, or speech difficulty
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for any sudden weakness, facial drooping, or speech difficulty, as rapid treatment improves outcomes.
notes: Time-critical condition; recognizing early signs and seeking immediate care is essential for the best outcome.

name: Chronic Kidney Disease
description: A progressive loss of kidney function over time, commonly caused by diabetes and hypertension.
keySymptoms: persistent swelling with fatigue in someone with diabetes or hypertension
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent swelling or fatigue, particularly with a history of diabetes or hypertension, for kidney function testing.
prevention: control of blood pressure and blood glucose
notes: Often progresses silently; regular screening is important in high-risk individuals.

name: Obesity
description: Excess body fat accumulation that increases the risk of numerous chronic diseases.
keySymptoms: body mass index above the healthy range on assessment
warningSigns: signs of related complications such as chest pain or severe breathlessness
whenToSeekCare: Seek guidance from a healthcare provider for weight assessment and management, particularly if other risk factors for chronic disease are present.
notes: A growing concern in urban Kenya, associated with rising rates of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

name: Sickle Cell Disease
description: An inherited blood disorder causing red blood cells to become rigid and sickle-shaped, leading to pain episodes and organ complications.
keySymptoms: recurrent episodes of severe bone or joint pain (vaso-occlusive crisis)
riskFactors: inherited sickle cell trait from both parents
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care during severe pain episodes or if fever, chest pain, or neurological symptoms develop, as these may indicate serious complications.
differentialConditions: other causes of acute severe pain
prevention: early diagnosis through newborn or family screening
hydration and avoiding known crisis triggers
notes: Requires long-term specialized management; infection and malaria can precipitate painful crises.

name: Cervical Cancer
description: A cancer arising from the cervix, strongly associated with persistent infection by certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).
keySymptoms: abnormal or postcoital vaginal bleeding in a woman with risk factors
whenToSeekCare: Seek gynecological evaluation for abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge, and participate in routine cervical cancer screening as recommended.
prevention: regular cervical cancer screening (Pap smear or HPV testing)
notes: One of the most common cancers among women in Kenya; screening programs are key to early detection.

name: Breast Cancer
description: A cancer that develops in breast tissue, one of the most common cancers among women.
commonSymptoms: change in breast shape or size
keySymptoms: a new, persistent, painless breast lump
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for any new breast lump or change, since early detection significantly improves outcomes.
prevention: breast self-awareness and clinical breast examination
notes: Late-stage presentation remains common in Kenya; awareness and early evaluation of breast changes are important.

name: Prostate Cancer
description: A cancer that develops in the prostate gland, common in older men.
keySymptoms: progressive urinary symptoms in an older man
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for new or worsening urinary symptoms in men over 50, or earlier with a family history.
prevention: discussion of screening options with a healthcare provider, particularly for those at higher risk
notes: One of the most commonly diagnosed cancers in men in Kenya; symptoms often overlap with benign prostate enlargement.

name: Esophageal Cancer
description: A cancer arising in the esophagus, notable for a comparatively high incidence in parts of Kenya, particularly the Rift Valley region.
keySymptoms: progressive difficulty swallowing, first with solids then liquids
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for progressive difficulty swallowing or unexplained weight loss.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: notably higher incidence reported in Rift Valley region
notes: One of the more common cancers in certain regions of Kenya; presentation is often at an advanced stage.

name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
description: An erosion of the lining of the stomach or duodenum, commonly linked to Helicobacter pylori infection or use of certain medications.
keySymptoms: burning epigastric pain related to meals
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent abdominal pain, and urgent care for vomiting blood or black stools.
prevention: H. pylori testing and treatment when indicated
notes: Complications such as bleeding or perforation require urgent medical attention.

name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
description: A condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation.
keySymptoms: burning chest discomfort related to meals or lying down
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation if symptoms are frequent, severe, or associated with difficulty swallowing or weight loss.
prevention: not lying down soon after eating
notes: Occasional reflux is common; frequent or severe symptoms warrant medical evaluation.

name: Osteoarthritis
description: A degenerative joint condition causing progressive breakdown of cartilage, most common in older adults.
keySymptoms: joint pain that worsens with activity and improves with rest
warningSigns: sudden severe joint swelling with fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent joint pain affecting daily activities, or urgently if a joint becomes suddenly hot, swollen, and painful.
notes: A common cause of chronic joint pain and disability in older adults.

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
description: A chronic autoimmune condition causing inflammation of the joints, typically affecting multiple joints symmetrically.
keySymptoms: symmetric joint swelling with prolonged morning stiffness
warningSigns: sudden severe joint swelling with fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent joint swelling and morning stiffness lasting more than a few weeks.
prevention: no established prevention; early diagnosis and treatment reduce joint damage
notes: Early treatment is important to prevent long-term joint damage and disability.

name: Epilepsy
description: A neurological condition characterized by recurrent, unprovoked seizures.
lessCommonSymptoms: loss of bladder control during a seizure
keySymptoms: recurrent unprovoked seizure episodes
warningSigns: repeated seizures without recovery in between
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation after a first seizure, and emergency care for a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes or repeated seizures.
prevention: prompt treatment of infections affecting the brain
notes: Stigma remains a barrier to care in many communities; consistent treatment substantially reduces seizure frequency.

name: Pre-eclampsia / Eclampsia
description: A pregnancy-related condition characterized by high blood pressure and organ involvement, which can progress to seizures (eclampsia) if untreated.
keySymptoms: new high blood pressure after 20 weeks of pregnancy with protein in urine
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency obstetric care immediately for severe headache, visual changes, or upper abdominal pain during pregnancy.
differentialConditions: other causes of headache in pregnancy
prevention: regular antenatal care with blood pressure monitoring
notes: A leading cause of maternal and perinatal mortality; regular antenatal visits allow early detection.

name: Postpartum Hemorrhage
description: Excessive bleeding following childbirth, a leading cause of maternal death if not promptly managed.
keySymptoms: bleeding exceeding normal amounts within 24 hours of delivery
whenToSeekCare: This is a medical emergency requiring immediate care at a health facility capable of emergency obstetric management.
prevention: active management of the third stage of labor
notes: A leading direct cause of maternal mortality in Kenya; delivery with a skilled attendant improves outcomes.

name: Ectopic Pregnancy
description: A pregnancy that implants outside the uterus, most commonly in a fallopian tube, which can become life-threatening if it ruptures.
keySymptoms: one-sided abdominal pain with a positive pregnancy test
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for abdominal pain with a positive pregnancy test, as rupture can cause life-threatening internal bleeding.
notes: A leading cause of first-trimester maternal death if not diagnosed and treated promptly.

name: Miscarriage (Spontaneous Abortion)
description: The loss of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive independently, most commonly occurring in the first trimester.
keySymptoms: vaginal bleeding with cramping in early pregnancy
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for any vaginal bleeding in pregnancy to determine the cause and appropriate management.
prevention: management of chronic conditions before pregnancy
notes: A common and often emotionally distressing pregnancy complication; prompt evaluation ensures safe management.

name: Anemia in Pregnancy
description: A reduction in red blood cells or hemoglobin during pregnancy, commonly due to iron deficiency, which can affect both mother and baby.
keySymptoms: progressive fatigue and paleness during pregnancy
whenToSeekCare: Attend routine antenatal visits for anemia screening; seek prompt care if severe fatigue or breathlessness develops.
prevention: iron and folic acid supplementation in pregnancy
notes: A common and largely preventable complication of pregnancy in Kenya; addressed through routine antenatal supplementation programs.

name: Gestational Diabetes
description: A form of high blood sugar that develops during pregnancy and usually resolves after delivery, but carries risks for mother and baby.
keySymptoms: elevated blood glucose identified on routine antenatal screening
warningSigns: signs of very high blood glucose such as confusion or severe dehydration
whenToSeekCare: Attend routine antenatal screening for gestational diabetes, and follow up as advised for blood glucose monitoring.
differentialConditions: pre-existing type 2 diabetes diagnosed in pregnancy
prevention: healthy diet and physical activity before and during pregnancy
notes: Increases the risk of type 2 diabetes later in life for the mother and requires monitoring during pregnancy.

name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
description: An infection of the female reproductive organs, often resulting from untreated sexually transmitted infections.
keySymptoms: lower abdominal pain with fever and abnormal discharge
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for pelvic pain with fever or abnormal discharge, as delayed treatment increases risk of infertility.
prevention: prompt treatment of sexually transmitted infections
notes: An important preventable cause of infertility and chronic pelvic pain if untreated.

name: Uterine Fibroids
description: Non-cancerous growths of the uterus, common among women of reproductive age.
keySymptoms: heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding with pelvic pressure
whenToSeekCare: Seek gynecological evaluation for heavy or prolonged periods or pelvic discomfort affecting daily life.
prevention: no established prevention; early evaluation of heavy bleeding allows timely management
notes: A very common benign gynecological condition; some cases require no treatment while others need medical or surgical management.

name: Infertility
description: The inability to conceive after a period of regular unprotected intercourse, which can result from factors affecting either partner.
commonSymptoms: difficulty conceiving after trying for one year or more
keySymptoms: absence of pregnancy despite regular unprotected intercourse over an extended period
riskFactors: male factors such as low sperm count
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation from a healthcare provider if pregnancy has not occurred after a year of regular unprotected intercourse, or sooner for women over 35.
prevention: prompt treatment of reproductive tract infections
notes: Both partners should be evaluated, as contributing factors can involve either or both.

name: Acute Diarrheal Disease in Children
description: Frequent loose or watery stools in a child, most commonly caused by viral, bacterial, or parasitic infection.
keySymptoms: increased stool frequency with looser consistency than usual
riskFactors: lack of exclusive breastfeeding in infants
warningSigns: signs of dehydration (sunken eyes, lethargy, reduced urine)
whenToSeekCare: Seek care promptly for signs of dehydration, blood in stool, or if the child cannot keep fluids down.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk in areas with limited clean water access
notes: A leading cause of childhood illness and death in Kenya; oral rehydration is a cornerstone of home and clinical management.

name: Pneumonia in Children
description: A lung infection in children, one of the leading causes of childhood illness and death globally and in Kenya.
keySymptoms: fast breathing or chest indrawing in a child with cough and fever
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical care for a child with fast or difficult breathing, chest indrawing, or reduced alertness.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk with indoor air pollution from cooking fuels
notes: A leading cause of death in children under five in Kenya; danger signs should prompt immediate care-seeking.

name: Kwashiorkor
description: A severe form of acute malnutrition caused primarily by insufficient protein intake, characterized by edema.
keySymptoms: bilateral pitting edema in a malnourished child
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care at a health facility for any child with swelling of the feet or body associated with poor nutrition, as specialized therapeutic feeding is needed.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk in food-insecure regions, including arid and semi-arid areas
prevention: exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months
continued breastfeeding with appropriate complementary feeding
notes: A medical emergency requiring management according to therapeutic feeding protocols at a health facility.

name: Marasmus
description: A severe form of acute malnutrition resulting from an overall deficiency of calories and nutrients, causing severe wasting.
keySymptoms: severe visible wasting without edema
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent care at a health facility for any child with severe visible wasting, as specialized therapeutic feeding is required.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: higher risk in food-insecure regions, including arid and semi-arid areas
prevention: exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months
notes: A medical emergency requiring management according to therapeutic feeding protocols at a health facility.

name: Neonatal Sepsis
description: A serious bloodstream infection occurring in the first 28 days of life, requiring urgent treatment.
keySymptoms: poor feeding with lethargy and temperature instability in a newborn
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for any newborn with poor feeding, lethargy, breathing difficulty, or temperature abnormality.
prevention: antenatal care to identify and treat maternal infections
notes: A leading cause of neonatal death; early recognition and urgent treatment are critical.

name: Rickets
description: A condition affecting bone development in children, most commonly due to vitamin D or calcium deficiency.
keySymptoms: bone deformities such as bowed legs in a young child
riskFactors: poor dietary calcium or vitamin D intake
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for a child with delayed growth or bone deformities for assessment and appropriate supplementation.
prevention: vitamin D and calcium sufficient diet
notes: Preventable through adequate nutrition and sunlight exposure; less common than infectious causes of childhood illness but clinically important.

name: Otitis Media
description: An infection of the middle ear, common in young children, often following an upper respiratory infection.
keySymptoms: ear pain or pulling at the ear with fever in a young child
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for ear pain with fever, and urgent care if swelling behind the ear or severe symptoms develop.
prevention: timely treatment of upper respiratory infections
notes: Usually resolves with appropriate care; recurrent episodes may need further evaluation.

name: Congenital Heart Disease
description: A structural heart abnormality present from birth, ranging from mild to severe in its effects on circulation.
lessCommonSymptoms: bluish discoloration of lips or skin
keySymptoms: bluish discoloration or breathlessness during feeding in an infant
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for an infant with poor feeding, poor growth, or breathlessness, as early diagnosis allows timely specialist care.
differentialConditions: other causes of failure to thrive
prevention: management of maternal conditions during pregnancy
avoiding known harmful exposures in pregnancy
notes: Severity varies widely; some forms require specialized surgical treatment, ideally identified early.

name: Iron Deficiency Anemia
description: A reduction in red blood cells due to inadequate iron, the most common cause of anemia worldwide.
keySymptoms: progressive fatigue and paleness with a diet low in iron-rich foods
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent fatigue and paleness for testing and identification of the underlying cause.
prevention: treatment of underlying causes of blood loss
notes: A common and largely treatable condition; identifying the underlying cause is important, especially in adults.

name: Vitamin A Deficiency
description: A nutritional deficiency that particularly affects vision and immune function, especially in young children.
keySymptoms: difficulty seeing in low light in a child with poor dietary diversity
riskFactors: inadequate dietary intake of vitamin A-rich foods
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for a child with poor night vision or eye changes to prevent progression to vision loss.
prevention: dietary diversity with vitamin A-rich foods
notes: A preventable cause of childhood blindness; supplementation programs are part of child health services in Kenya.

name: Iodine Deficiency Disorder (Goiter)
description: A condition resulting from insufficient dietary iodine, which can cause thyroid enlargement and developmental problems.
commonSymptoms: swelling in the front of the neck (goiter)
keySymptoms: visible or palpable neck swelling in front of the throat
riskFactors: living in an area with iodine-poor soil
warningSigns: difficulty breathing or swallowing due to a large goiter
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for neck swelling for assessment of thyroid function.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: certain inland and highland areas with iodine-poor soil
notes: Largely preventable through universal salt iodization programs.

name: Depression
description: A common mental health condition characterized by persistent sadness and loss of interest, affecting daily functioning.
keySymptoms: persistent low mood or loss of interest lasting most of the day for two weeks or more
whenToSeekCare: Seek support from a healthcare provider or counselor if low mood persists most of the day for two weeks or more, or immediately if there are thoughts of self-harm.
notes: Often under-recognized and stigmatized; this is a sensitive topic and support resources should be offered if someone appears to be struggling personally.

name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
description: A mental health condition characterized by excessive, persistent worry that is difficult to control.
keySymptoms: persistent, excessive worry across multiple areas of life lasting six months or more
warningSigns: panic symptoms with chest pain (should be assessed to rule out cardiac causes)
inability to function in daily life
whenToSeekCare: Seek support from a healthcare provider or counselor if worry is persistent, excessive, and interferes with daily functioning.
notes: Physical symptoms of anxiety can mimic other medical conditions, so appropriate evaluation is important.

name: Alcohol Use Disorder
description: A pattern of alcohol use that leads to significant impairment or distress, ranging from harmful use to dependence.
keySymptoms: loss of control over drinking with continued use despite negative consequences
whenToSeekCare: Seek support from a healthcare provider or counseling and support services; withdrawal from heavy long-term use may require medical supervision.
prevention: access to counseling and support services
notes: This is a sensitive topic; a supportive, non-judgmental approach and connection to appropriate services is important.

name: Substance Use Disorder (Other Drugs)
description: A pattern of use of drugs other than alcohol that leads to significant impairment or distress.
commonSymptoms: strong urges to use the substance
keySymptoms: loss of control over substance use with continued use despite negative consequences
warningSigns: signs of overdose (unconsciousness, severe breathing difficulty)
whenToSeekCare: Seek support from a healthcare provider or counseling and support services; some withdrawal states require medical supervision.
prevention: access to counseling and rehabilitation services
notes: This is a sensitive topic; a supportive, non-judgmental approach and connection to appropriate services is important.

name: Schizophrenia
description: A chronic mental health condition affecting a person's thinking, perception, and behavior, often including hallucinations or delusions.
keySymptoms: persistent hallucinations or fixed false beliefs affecting daily functioning
warningSigns: risk of harm to self or others
complete inability to care for oneself
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt evaluation from a mental health professional for persistent hallucinations, delusions, or significant behavioral changes.
prevention: early intervention when symptoms first appear
notes: Long-term management with consistent care and social support significantly improves quality of life; stigma remains a major barrier to care.

name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
description: A mental health condition that can develop after exposure to a traumatic or life-threatening event.
keySymptoms: persistent re-experiencing of a traumatic event with avoidance and hyperarousal symptoms
riskFactors: exposure to trauma, violence, accidents, or disaster
lack of social support after trauma
warningSigns: inability to function in daily life
whenToSeekCare: Seek support from a mental health professional if symptoms persist for more than a month after a traumatic event or significantly affect daily life.
prevention: early psychosocial support after traumatic events
notes: This is a sensitive topic; a calm, supportive approach and connection to appropriate resources is important.

name: Bipolar Disorder
description: A mental health condition characterized by alternating episodes of depression and mania or hypomania.
commonSymptoms: periods of elevated or irritable mood
changes in energy and activity levels
reduced need for sleep during manic episodes
keySymptoms: distinct episodes of markedly elevated or irritable mood alternating with depressive episodes
warningSigns: reckless or dangerous behavior during mania
whenToSeekCare: Seek evaluation from a mental health professional for episodes of unusually elevated mood or energy, or for persistent depressive symptoms.
notes: Requires ongoing specialist management; untreated manic episodes can lead to significant personal and social harm.

name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
description: A chronic inflammatory skin condition causing itchy, dry, and inflamed skin, often starting in childhood.
keySymptoms: chronic itchy rash in typical flexural areas (elbow and knee creases)
riskFactors: family history of eczema, asthma, or allergies
whenToSeekCare: Most cases can be managed with regular skin care; seek medical attention if the skin becomes infected or the rash is severe and unresponsive to care.
notes: A chronic relapsing condition; management focuses on skin barrier care and trigger avoidance.

name: Psoriasis
description: A chronic autoimmune skin condition causing thick, scaly patches, with a relapsing and remitting course.
keySymptoms: well-demarcated red plaques with silvery scale, often on elbows and knees
warningSigns: signs of joint involvement with swelling
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent scaly skin patches for diagnosis and management, especially if joint symptoms develop.
notes: A chronic condition requiring long-term management; can be associated with joint involvement in some individuals.

name: Acne Vulgaris
description: A common skin condition involving the hair follicles and oil glands, most frequent during adolescence.
keySymptoms: pimples, blackheads, and whiteheads concentrated on the face, chest, or back
whenToSeekCare: Most cases can be managed with routine skin care; seek medical evaluation for severe or scarring acne that does not improve with basic measures.
notes: Very common during adolescence and often improves with age; early treatment can reduce scarring risk.

name: Low Back Pain
description: Pain in the lower back, one of the most common musculoskeletal complaints, usually related to muscle strain or mechanical factors.
keySymptoms: pain related to movement or posture without neurological symptoms
warningSigns: loss of bladder or bowel control
whenToSeekCare: Most cases improve with rest and gentle activity; seek urgent care if there is leg weakness, numbness in the groin area, or loss of bladder or bowel control.
notes: Most low back pain is mechanical and self-limiting, but warning signs should prompt urgent evaluation.

name: Gout
description: A form of inflammatory arthritis caused by the buildup of uric acid crystals in joints, often affecting the big toe.
keySymptoms: sudden onset of severe pain, redness, and swelling in a single joint, often the big toe
riskFactors: diet high in purines (red meat, certain seafood)
warningSigns: high fever with joint swelling (to rule out joint infection)
multiple joints affected simultaneously with systemic illness
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for sudden severe joint pain and swelling, particularly if this is a first episode, to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection.
notes: Recurrent attacks can lead to joint damage if underlying uric acid levels are not managed long-term.

name: Migraine
description: A recurrent headache disorder characterized by moderate to severe throbbing pain, often with associated symptoms.
keySymptoms: recurrent throbbing headaches with nausea and light sensitivity
warningSigns: headache with fever and neck stiffness
whenToSeekCare: Seek routine care for recurrent headaches affecting daily life, and urgent care for a sudden severe headache unlike previous episodes or with neurological symptoms.
notes: A common cause of recurrent disabling headache; distinguishing from more serious causes of headache is important.

name: Tension-Type Headache
description: The most common type of headache, typically described as a dull, band-like pressure around the head.
lessCommonSymptoms: mild sensitivity to light or sound
keySymptoms: bilateral, non-throbbing headache without significant nausea
warningSigns: sudden severe headache unlike usual pattern
headache with fever and neck stiffness
whenToSeekCare: Most cases can be managed with rest and stress reduction; seek medical evaluation if headaches become frequent, severe, or change in character.
notes: Usually mild to moderate and self-limiting; frequent episodes may benefit from professional evaluation.

name: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy
description: Nerve damage affecting the extremities, a common complication of long-standing or poorly controlled diabetes.
keySymptoms: symmetric numbness and tingling in the feet in a person with diabetes
whenToSeekCare: Seek regular diabetes follow-up care including foot examinations, and prompt evaluation for any foot wound or infection given reduced sensation.
notes: Reduced sensation increases the risk of unnoticed foot injuries and subsequent complications; regular foot checks are important.

name: Childhood Leukemia
description: A cancer of the blood and bone marrow, the most common form of childhood cancer.
keySymptoms: persistent unexplained paleness, bruising, and fatigue in a child
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for a child with unexplained persistent paleness, bruising, or fatigue, as early diagnosis improves outcomes.
prevention: no established prevention; early recognition and referral improve outcomes
notes: Requires urgent referral to a specialized pediatric oncology center for diagnosis and treatment.

name: Anthrax
description: A bacterial zoonotic infection that can affect the skin, lungs, or gastrointestinal tract, usually acquired from infected livestock or their products.
commonSymptoms: skin sore that develops into a painless black ulcer
keySymptoms: painless black-centered skin ulcer following contact with livestock or animal products
riskFactors: contact with sick or dead livestock
handling contaminated animal hides or meat
consumption of meat from infected animals
warningSigns: severe abdominal pain with vomiting blood
whenToSeekCare: Seek urgent medical care for any unusual skin ulcer after animal contact, or illness following consumption of meat from a sick animal.
prevention: avoiding contact with sick or dead animals
proper handling and cooking of meat
notes: Occurs sporadically in association with livestock disease outbreaks; prompt treatment is important given its potential severity.

name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
description: A non-cancerous enlargement of the prostate gland, common in older men, which can obstruct urine flow.
keySymptoms: progressive urinary symptoms in an older man without other systemic symptoms
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for bothersome or worsening urinary symptoms, and urgent care for inability to urinate.
prevention: no established prevention; routine evaluation of urinary symptoms in older men
notes: A very common condition in older men; symptoms overlap with prostate cancer, so evaluation is recommended.

name: Kidney Stones (Nephrolithiasis)
description: Hard mineral deposits that form in the kidneys and can cause severe pain when passing through the urinary tract.
keySymptoms: sudden severe colicky flank pain radiating toward the groin
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical care for severe flank pain, especially with fever or inability to urinate, which may indicate a urinary obstruction with infection.
prevention: dietary modification based on stone type when known
notes: Pain from kidney stones can be severe; fever accompanying an obstructing stone is a urological emergency.

name: Urinary Incontinence
description: The involuntary leakage of urine, which can result from various underlying causes and becomes more common with age.
keySymptoms: involuntary urine loss affecting daily activities
warningSigns: complete inability to control urination with associated neurological symptoms
new-onset incontinence with back pain and leg weakness
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation as incontinence is often treatable once the underlying cause is identified.
notes: Often under-reported due to embarrassment, though effective treatments are usually available.

name: Anaphylaxis
description: A severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that occurs rapidly after exposure to an allergen.
keySymptoms: rapid onset of breathing difficulty or throat swelling after allergen exposure
warningSigns: swelling of the throat or tongue
whenToSeekCare: This is a medical emergency — seek immediate emergency care for any signs of difficulty breathing or throat swelling after a possible allergen exposure.
prevention: carrying emergency treatment as prescribed for known severe allergies
notes: Requires immediate emergency treatment; can be rapidly fatal without prompt intervention.

name: Snake Bite Envenomation
description: Injury from a venomous snake bite that can cause local tissue damage and, in some cases, life-threatening systemic effects.
commonSymptoms: pain and swelling at the bite site
keySymptoms: bite marks with progressive local swelling following snake exposure
riskFactors: living or working in rural or bush areas
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency medical care immediately for any snake bite; keep the affected limb still and avoid traditional remedies or cutting the wound while seeking care.
seasonalOrGeographicFactors: rural and bush areas, particularly in agricultural and pastoral regions
prevention: wearing protective footwear in high-risk areas
caution when working in vegetation or handling firewood
notes: Antivenom availability and appropriate first aid are important; traditional treatments such as wound cutting or tourniquets are not recommended.

name: Burns
description: Tissue injury caused by heat, chemicals, electricity, or friction, ranging from minor to life-threatening depending on extent and depth.
keySymptoms: burn injury with a clear causative exposure (heat, chemical, electrical)
riskFactors: unsafe use of paraffin or gas stoves
warningSigns: burns covering a large body surface area
burns to the face, hands, or genitals
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical care for any burn larger than a small area, burns to sensitive areas, or if there are signs of infection or breathing difficulty; cool the burn with running water and avoid home remedies like oils or toothpaste.
prevention: keeping flammable materials away from children
notes: A common household injury, particularly among young children in kitchen settings; prompt appropriate first aid improves outcomes.

name: Road Traffic Injury / Trauma
description: Physical injury resulting from road traffic collisions, a major cause of injury and death, particularly among young adults.
commonSymptoms: pain at the site of injury
keySymptoms: injury with a clear traumatic mechanism (collision, fall from a vehicle)
riskFactors: lack of seatbelt or helmet use
whenToSeekCare: Seek emergency care immediately for any significant road traffic injury, particularly with head injury, severe bleeding, or suspected fracture.
prevention: avoiding driving under the influence of alcohol
notes: A leading cause of injury and death among young adults in Kenya; emergency transport and care systems are critical to outcomes.

name: Dental Caries
description: Tooth decay caused by bacterial breakdown of tooth structure, one of the most common chronic conditions worldwide.
keySymptoms: localized tooth pain associated with a visible cavity or dark spot on the tooth
warningSigns: difficulty swallowing or breathing due to spreading infection
whenToSeekCare: Seek dental care for persistent tooth pain, and urgent care if facial swelling or fever develops, as this may indicate a spreading dental infection.
prevention: regular tooth brushing with fluoride toothpaste
reducing sugary food and drink intake
notes: Highly prevalent and largely preventable; access to dental care can be limited in some areas.
